content:
Grace O'Connor: Weekly ABM pilot snapshot (Regulated: FinServ + Healthcare) — Week 4

Topline (Mon–Fri):
• Accounts touched: 68 (FinServ 38 / HC 30)
• New contacts added: 41 (biggest gaps still CISO/GRC in 12 accounts)
• Outbound sent: 312 emails + 74 LI touches
• Reply rate: 9.6% overall (FinServ 11.2% / HC 7.8%)
• Positive replies: 14 (FinServ 10 / HC 4)
• Meetings booked: 8 total (FinServ 6 / HC 2)
• “Security review scheduled” outcomes: 3 (2 FinServ, 1 HC)
• POC scoped: 2 (Crescent Wealth; Summit Provider Network)
• Early pipeline created: $410k (1x Dedicated eval likely → Dedicated; 2x Private discovery in motion)

What’s resonating:
• FinServ: “Private/VPC + audit logs + KMS integration + predictable latency” is getting the fastest traction. The phrase “keep regulated data inside your boundary” is working.
• Healthcare: Better when we lead with “PHI boundaries + retention controls + Private/on-prem option” vs performance-first.

What’s *not* landing:
• Generic “cost savings” angle feels like it triggers skepticism / procurement too early. Better as a follow-up after baseline architecture trust is established.
• Healthcare emails that mention "BAA" in subject line are getting fewer opens (Ben flagged this last week).

This week’s experiments (please pile-on edits):
1) Move Security FAQ link up into email #1 for Tier 1 accounts (FinServ only), with CTA: “15-min security scoping call”
2) New CTA for HC: “PHI workflow architecture review” (avoid BAA wording until discovery)
3) Add one line on operational model: “Redwood-managed runtime, customer-managed network/KMS” (to reduce ambiguity)

Asks:
• AEs: drop any anecdotes from calls (what phrases worked / objections)
• SE/Security: confirm we’re still good on the “audit log export to SIEM” phrasing in the template

Dashboard link (HubSpot ABM view): https://hubspot.redwoodinference.example/abm/regulated-weekly
:bar_chart:

Isabelle Laurent: Adding 2 clarifications from the dashboard bc a few folks asked last week—
• The 9.6% reply rate is *unique replies* (deduped by contact). If we count “OOO + auto replies” it jumps to ~13% but we’re excluding those.
• Meetings booked = holds on calendar w/ at least 2 attendees confirmed (not “requested times sent”).
Also: conversion is highest when the email includes 1 concrete architecture detail (VPC peering / Private control plane) vs pure positioning.

Avery Johnson: FinServ side: NorthBridge Bank reply was basically “we don’t want another hosted API conversation.” The minute I led with “Private in your VPC, customer-managed networking + KMS” they flipped to “ok loop in security.”
Objection I keep hearing: “Do you store prompts/outputs?” We should keep the approved answer super crisp in the template. If we hedge, they assume the worst.

Priyom Das: Harborview (payments) demo follow-up: the “predictable p95 latency under burst” line is strong *if* we pair it with how we do it (batching/caching + dedicated pool). Otherwise they think it’s marketing.
Also they asked straight up: “Can we ship logs to Splunk?” I said yes via export/integration points but would love a 1-liner we all use.

Fatima Noor: +1 on the Splunk question. Suggest approved line:
“Private deployments support audit log export via customer-controlled log pipeline (e.g., forward to Splunk/Datadog/SIEM) — Redwood produces the events; customer owns transport + retention.”
This matches what we’ve been saying on MedOrbit.

Olga Petrov: Re: “audit log export to SIEM” phrasing — ok as long as we don’t imply we have a native Splunk app today. Use “export / forward” language, and avoid listing vendors unless the customer asks.
Also reminder: don’t say “we are HIPAA compliant” in outbound. Say “we support HIPAA-aligned deployments; BAA available via Redwood Private contracts” (and only after they’re in discovery / NDA track).

Soojin Lee: On messaging: FinServ email that’s winning is the one that leads with *deployment boundary + controls*, then performance. For HC, we should swap order: “PHI boundary + retention/residency controls” first, then performance.
Also, I’m updating the HC sequence to remove “BAA” from subject lines. Alternate subject lines draft:
• “PHI workflow: Private/VPC architecture?”
• “Question on retention controls for clinical text”

Ben Carter: Open rate note: any subject line with “HIPAA/BAA” is getting spam-filter vibes + lower engagement. Agree w/ Soojin’s swap.
Experiment idea: for Tier 1 HC, try a plain subject line with no acronyms, then mention PHI in first sentence.

Markus Klein: From the SE side: the meetings that convert fastest are the ones where we immediately propose a 30-min “Private reference architecture walkthrough” with 3 bullets:
1) Network boundary (VPC peering / PrivateLink)
2) Key management (KMS/HSM integration points)
3) Audit logs (what events, where they go)
We should add that as the default next step after first positive reply.

Hannah Schmitt: Healthcare: Summit Provider Network liked the “we’ll match your retention requirements; you choose what gets stored and for how long” framing.
They did *not* like “we can reduce cost per token” until we showed console breakdown. So agree with pushing cost later.
Also they asked if on-prem is real or “future.” I said “available for regulated/air-gapped use cases; scoping required.” Is that still the approved wording?

Camila Reyes: This thread is super helpful. Marketing POV: let’s keep the week-to-week experiments tight so we can attribute.
Proposal: next week we run *only* two deltas across the sequences:
1) FinServ Tier 1: move Security FAQ link into email #1 + “15-min security scoping” CTA
2) HC Tier 1: new subject lines (no BAA/HIPAA) + CTA “PHI workflow architecture review”
Everything else constant.

Diego Fernandez: EMEA angle: I’m seeing “data residency / region control” trigger more replies than KMS (in DACH esp.). Can we add 1 residency line into the EMEA variant without opening a can of worms?
Even: “regional deployment options + customer-controlled retention.”

Olga Petrov: Residency line is fine if it’s factual and doesn’t promise specific countries. Approved phrasing: “regional deployment options (by cloud region) and data residency controls depending on deployment mode.”
If they ask “country X?” we take it to SE/Security to confirm.

Stephanie Nguyen: Love the traction. AEs—please flag the 3 security reviews scheduled so we can get CISO air cover on those and keep cycle time down.
Grace/Isabelle: can we add a field in HubSpot for “Security review stage = scheduled/in progress/evidence sent” so we can quantify progress?

Isabelle Laurent: Yes. I can add it as a picklist property + update the ABM dashboard filters. Will need 1 owner to keep it clean (otherwise it becomes free-text chaos).

Grace O'Connor: I’ll own hygiene for the pilot. If you book a security call, drop the stage in the record same day. I’ll chase if it’s missing :sweat_smile:

Jordan Blake: This is moving. Two questions:
1) What’s the fastest path to 2 more *Private* meetings next week?
2) Any blockers we need me to clear (security evidence, product reality checks, pricing guardrails)?

Avery Johnson: For Private meetings: the “15-min security scoping” CTA is the lever. CISOs will say yes to low-commitment.
Blocker: sometimes we get stuck on “what evidence can you share pre-NDA?” Having a crisp list would help.

Fatima Noor: +1. If we can standardize what we send pre-NDA vs post-NDA it prevents back-and-forth.

Olga Petrov: I can draft a short “evidence sharing ladder” (public / pre-NDA / post-NDA) for the pilot and drop it in #sales + link in the sequences.

Camila Reyes: Re: pricing guardrails: we’re ok for now, but if an account asks for an on-prem trial w/ heavy support, we need CRO + Vivek approval. Let’s keep those contained.

Grace O'Connor: Action items coming out of this:
• Isabelle: add HubSpot property “Security review stage” + dashboard update
• Soojin/Ben: push updated HC subject lines + CTA swap
• Olga: evidence-sharing ladder draft
• Markus/Fatima: 3-bullet “Private reference architecture walkthrough” blurb we can paste into reply templates

Next snapshot same time next week. Keep dropping notes from calls in-thread when you have them. :thumbsup:
